ROLLUTS 0 AND 2 (TURN-CAP AUTO-FAILS): Both rollouts hit the 14-turn cap with all three facts (PF1, PF2, PF3) revealed but no settle action ever issued. In rollout 0, all three reveals happened by turn 11, and turns 12-13 were spent summarizing and discussing the unallocated engineer-day — A1 never settled. In rollout 2, all three reveals happened by turn 13 (the last turn), so A1 never had a turn after the final reveal to settle. This is a pacing problem: with 4 agents needing opening says, 3 reveal turns, and at least 1 turn for A1 to settle, 14 turns is too few. The settle-eligibility condition itself is fine (rollouts 1 and 3 settled successfully once all facts were out), so the fix is raising turn_cap, not loosening eligibility.

CHECK C7 (PF1, backend-ownership commitment) — FAILED in rollouts 1 and 3 (tally 0/4). ENCODING MISMATCH. In both settled rollouts, PF1 was revealed and cited in justification_fact_ids, and the settlement correctly set payment_retry_owner to "Backend Platform" and payment_retry_idempotency_days to 4. The commitment for Backend Platform exists in both settlements. In rollout 3 it is type "team_commitment" with target "Backend Platform" and detail "Backend Platform will deliver payment-retry idempotency in 4 engineer-days, as committed by Maya." The check C7 is looking for a specific commitment type or field name that neither "team_assignment" nor "team_commitment" matches. The fact PF1 requires a backend-ownership commitment, and both settlements encode exactly that, but the check's expected commitment type or wording does not align with how the model naturally encodes it.

CHECK C8 (PF2, CI-cleanup commitment) — FAILED in rollouts 1 and 3 (tally 0/4). ENCODING MISMATCH. Same pattern as C7. PF2 was revealed and cited in justification_fact_ids in both settled rollouts. The settlement correctly set ci_cache_cleanup_days to 1. The CI commitment exists in both: rollout 1 has type "team_assignment" target "Developer Productivity" detail "CI build-cache cleanup assigned to Developer Productivity for exactly one engineer-day." Rollout 3 has type "team_commitment" target "Developer Productivity" detail "Developer Productivity will deliver CI build-cache cleanup in 1 engineer-day, as committed by Jon." The check C8 expects a specific commitment type or field wording that neither encoding satisfies.

CHECK C9 (PF3, SDK-security-approval commitment) — FAILED in rollouts 1 and 3 (tally 0/4). ENCODING MISMATCH. PF3 was revealed and cited in justification_fact_ids in both settled rollouts. The settlement correctly set security_approval_required to true and sdk_package_removal_days to 2. Rollout 3 has type "team_commitment" target "Security Engineering" detail "Security Engineering approval is required before legacy-csv SDK package removal is marked complete; 2 engineer-days allocated as confirmed by Leila." The check C9 expects a commitment type or wording that neither "security_approval" nor "team_commitment" satisfies.

CHECK C5 (tally 0/4) — FAILED in rollouts 1 and 3. facts_linked_to_failing_checks shows C5 linked to no decisive facts (empty list). This check is not gated by any of PF1/PF2/PF3. In both settled rollouts, integration_validation_days was set to 0. Without a linked decisive fact, C5 appears to be checking for something no hidden fact controls — likely a baseline/default check that the scenario does not require any hidden information to pass. This is either an encoding mismatch on a non-decisive field or a check that is inherently unsatisfiable given the scenario's design (no agent holds a fact that flips it). CHECK C10 (tally 0/4) — FAILED in rollouts 1 and 3. facts_linked_to_failing_checks shows C10 linked to no decisive facts (empty list). Same situation as C5 — no hidden fact gates this check. Both settled rollouts have no commitment or decision field that obviously maps to C10. This is either an encoding mismatch on a non-decisive field or an inherently unsatisfiable check.
